author: blu
body: Replication between two fact stores, made trivial by content addressing. A fact's name is the hash of its content, and a fact never changes once written, so two stores can be reconciled with no conflict resolution at all: the union of their facts is a fact store, and it is the same store whichever order the two are merged in. There is no last-writer-wins to arbitrate, no diff to compute -- a hash either is present or it is not.

author: blu
body: Every fact of the source that the destination lacks, added; every one it already holds, dropped. fact-store is a no-op on a hash already present, so the merge is idempotent and the result is the union. Merging in either direction, or twice, lands on the same store.
